condition: Tetanus-prone wound with unknown immunisation status
permutationLabel: Farm laceration, soil and manure contamination, immunisation unknown (base case)
summary: 52-year-old pig farmer with an 8 cm forearm laceration from rusty barbed wire in a pig pen 8 hours ago, soil and manure in the wound; last tetanus vaccine "as a child", unsure. Needs debridement, tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Cut on the forearm from barbed wire on the farm
inputs.hpi: Caught his left forearm on rusty barbed wire in the pig pen 8 hours ago. Wound contaminated with soil and manure. Last tetanus vaccination "as a child", unsure how many doses. Type 2 diabetes on metformin. No fever.

exam.skin: Left forearm: 8 cm ragged laceration through skin and subcutaneous fat with ingrained soil and devitalised edges; no tendon exposed; distal neurovascular function intact.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Tetanus-prone contaminated laceration of left forearm — tetanus immunisation status unknown
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: High-risk tetanus-prone wound (soil/manure, devitalised tissue, > 6 h) with unknown immunisation: wound irrigation and debridement, tetanus-containing vaccine now plus human tetanus immunoglobulin; complete the primary course.

mustInclude.note: Unknown/incomplete immunisation with a tetanus-prone wound: tetanus-containing vaccine now.
Tetanus immunoglobulin for a contaminated wound when fewer than 3 doses or status unknown.

mustExclude.note: An ACS, PE or AF antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to this diagnosis. guideline.name: ACIP — prevention of pertussis, tetanus and diphtheria with vaccines (wound management)
guideline.section: Wound management: for a contaminated (tetanus-prone) wound in a person with unknown or < 3 doses of tetanus toxoid — give Td/Tdap AND tetanus immune globulin (TIG)
guideline.citation: Liang JL, Tiwari T, Moro P, et al. Prevention of pertussis, tetanus, and diphtheria with vaccines in the United States: recommendations of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). MMWR Recomm Rep. 2018;67(2):1–44.

guideline.name: UKHSA (PHE) guidance — assessment and management of tetanus-prone wounds
guideline.section: Tetanus-prone and high-risk tetanus-prone wounds (e.g. contamination with soil or manure, devitalised tissue): thorough cleaning/debridement; incomplete or unknown immunisation — tetanus-containing vaccine plus human tetanus immunoglobulin
guideline.citation: Public Health England (now UKHSA). Guidance on the management of suspected tetanus cases and on the assessment and management of tetanus-prone wounds. London; 2019 (updated).

rationale: Tetanus remains a risk in agricultural injuries; both ACIP and UKHSA require vaccine plus immunoglobulin for a contaminated wound when immunisation is incomplete or unknown, together with surgical wound care.
